BiblicalUsage: Adiyn means voluptuous — given to pleasure, soft and self-indulgent — and it appears only once, in God's judgment on Babylon: 'thou that art given to pleasures, that dwellest carelessly, that sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me.' The word paints a city drunk on its own comfort, certain that nothing can touch it, on the very edge of ruin.
TheologicalSignificance: I won't force this word to carry more than it was written to carry; the teaching lives in its verse, and that is enough; in this case, the verse is Isaiah 47:8.
